perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s available perspective:

- Ethan is a plumber. Gary Guo is his long-time friend from middle school; they are close and rely on each other for support.
- Ethan knows Gary is a doctor. He noticed Gary working excessively long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep, and he became concerned about Gary’s health.
- Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation. Gary initially said he appreciated the concern but couldn’t because of hospital work. Ethan later observed Gary at the retreat.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than just professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school and that Gary could tell him anything without judgment.
- Gary told Ethan it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden him.
- Gary then opened up to Ethan about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. Specific details beyond that are not provided.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges. Ethan saw Gary making efforts to change.
- Gary told Ethan things were better, he was less overwhelmed, and he had time for a movie.
- After about a year, Ethan saw Gary had adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and could manage on his own.
- Ethan told Gary he was always just a call away and knew Gary had it. Gary thanked Ethan, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.
- Ethan’s own reactions during this: concern, suspicion, relief/empathy, hope/pride, and satisfaction/happiness.
